text:
Ben (sales): Nora from Acme POC reporting intermittent 429s on /v1/generate today, mostly when they hit a burst of chat requests. Tenant usage looks under the committed quota. Can SRE + SE triage?
Aisha (sales-eng): copying logs + quick checklist: can you paste the exact request headers and a sample response (with x-rw-* headers)? Also, are they hitting multiple routes?
Nora (Acme): pasting minimal curl and the 429 body we see. This happens ~every 30-90s during tests.
Nora (Acme): ```bash
curl -i -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-acme" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small-rl","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2024 18:05:12 GMT
x-rw-rate-limit: 25;w=1;burst=50
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 7
content-type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"route capacity exceeded","code":429}}
```
Ben (sales): they run a quick stress test script that opens a few concurrent streams, so bursts are expected. Tenant-level quota shows 12M tokens left.
Derek (SRE): that x-rw-rate-limit header shows a per-route cap of 25 r/s and burst window 50 — looks like route-level limiter is the blocker, not tenant budget. Do we know which route the POC is hitting?
Nora (Acme): they use the default route for /v1/generate (route id r-acme-default) per account. We didn't change route caps.
Aisha (sales-eng): possible mismatch: sales reserved tenant credits but didn't request per-route bump. For demos we usually set a temporary per-route softcap increase.
Jules (infra): quick check command to view route config (internal API):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routes/r-acme-default | jq -r '.rate_limit'
# returns: {"per_second":25,"burst":50,"mode":"strict"}
```
Derek (SRE): yep that's it. The infra default for new POCs is conservative. Options: 1) raise per_second to 200 with burst 500 for 1hr, 2) set mode to "reservations" and allocate tokens from tenant pool, or 3) add a soft quota that allows short bursts above cap. Which do we want?
Ben (sales): client expects demo today at 20:00 UTC. Short-term fix needed. Also want to avoid permanent cost surprises.
Aisha (sales-eng): short-term: bump per-route to 200/500 for 2 hours. Medium: submit reservations request for next demos. Long-term: update presales checklist so per-route bump is requested automatically for trial accounts > X concurrent streams.
Derek (SRE): I'll patch now. Executing admin change:
```bash
# admin action (internal)
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routes/r-acme-default \ 
  -d '{"rate_limit":{"per_second":200,"burst":500,"mode":"soft"},"note":"Presales bump - Ben/Acme POC"}'
```
QuotaBot: route r-acme-default rate_limit change proposed by Derek at 2024-07-17T18:10:45Z (per_second:25->200, burst:50->500). Confirm yes/no.
Aisha (sales-eng): +1 approve from SE to proceed.
Jules (infra): applying change now. Patch returns 200 OK.
Jules (infra): ```json
{"route_id":"r-acme-default","rate_limit":{"per_second":200,"burst":500,"mode":"soft"},"updated_by":"derek"}
```
Nora (Acme): deploying new load script now to validate. Will run 300 concurrent short requests for 5m.
Nora (Acme): first 2 minutes look clean, no 429s. Thanks! :tada:
Derek (SRE): leaving the soft mode for 2 hours; will auto-revert at 20:15 UTC. Logging note added to the route.
Ben (sales): great, please make the mid-term reservation workflow PR. Also tell finance to expect a temporary bump in usage for that account.
Aisha (sales-eng): filing a checklist ticket: set per-route bump + record in POC playbook + presales automation.
Nora (Acme): post-run stats: 5m steady, peak 450 r/s, 0 429s, latency ~120ms median. Thank you all.
Derek (SRE): root cause summary: per-route hard cap (25 r/s) was lower than expected for demo bursts. Tenant credits were unused but not surfaced to route-level limiter. Fix: temporary per-route bump + follow-up automation to reserve per-route capacity for demos.
Ben (sales): closing this thread — will follow up on automation ticket later. :white_check_mark:
